Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: I registered a first round of genotype- and pathway-anchored comparisons before seeing evidence. For oncogene-driven outcomes, I expect exposure to the cognate activating alteration to produce stronger dependency (a more negative CRISPR score, hence a negative raw mean difference and negative hypothesis direction): KRAS mutation with KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E with BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification with EGFR dependency, and ERBB2 amplification with ERBB2 dependency. Alternative explanations include pathway bypass, redundant RTK/MAPK inputs, or non-cell-autonomous screening artifacts. For MDM2, I expect TP53 loss to weaken MDM2 dependency because MDM2's main vulnerability is degradation of wild-type p53; thus the raw mean difference should be positive/less negative, so I registered direction +1. For SMARCA2, SMARCA4 loss is a well-known paralog-dependency context, so I expect stronger SMARCA2 dependency (negative direction). For WRN, MSI-high cell lines are a well-supported WRN-dependent context, so I expect stronger WRN dependency (negative direction). For NFE2L2, KEAP1 loss should constitutively activate NRF2 signaling and may create dependence on NFE2L2 activity, yielding a negative expected contrast; an alternative is that NFE2L2 dependency reflects its own mutation rather than KEAP1 loss. For MYC amplification, I proposed dependencies on USP7, DHX9, and POLR2A: MYC-driven cells may rely on deubiquitinase-mediated MYC/MDM2 regulation, transcription/chromatin helicase activity, and core RNA polymerase II function due to transcription stress. EGFR amplification may also increase STAT3 dependency through RTK-associated inflammatory signaling. These are not causal claims yet; initial status is unresolved pending effect size and uncertainty.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum

For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct

expectation

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

record.narrative:
The first analysis round provides two very strong dataset associations and one very strong reversal. Because estimates are already signed to the registered direction, positive estimates support the claim and negative estimates contradict it. H6 (SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA2 dependency) has a signed difference of +0.784, 95% CI [0.765,0.803]; given the very negative CRISPR score means stronger dependency, this corresponds to a huge raw decrease in SMARCA2 dependency in SMARCA4-loss cells. The magnitude is far above the SD of SMARCA2 scores and is clinically important under a 10% relative-change standard. H7 (MSI-high versus WRN dependency) is similarly strong: +0.790, CI [0.760,0.819], supporting stronger WRN dependency in MSI-high cells. These effects are so large that multiplicity, cell-count adequacy, and baseline-scale concerns do not materially threaten their interpretation as associations in this dataset; they are still not causal claims.

H8 is the clearest opposite signal. For KEAP1 loss versus NFE2L2 dependency, the registered expectation was stronger NFE2L2 dependency (direction -1), but the signed estimate is -0.796 with CI [-0.816,-0.776]. Since direction is -1, this means the raw contrast is strongly positive: KEAP1-loss cells have weaker or positive NFE2L2 dependency. Thus H8 is rejected as stated, but the finding justifies a registered reversal for later formal evaluation.

H3 is borderline but biologically and clinically interesting: EGFR amplification versus EGFR dependency has a positive signed estimate of +0.025, CI [-0.00025,0.051]. If the comparator mean is near the overall mean around -0.25, the point estimate is roughly a 10% stronger dependency, and the upper bound is well above 10%, while the lower bound just crosses zero. This is not sufficient to accept now, so I request independent validation of H3 because it is the claim where an independent interval is most likely to change the conclusion.

The remaining null or near-null results are mostly low priority. H1 is imprecise but small: the expected KRAS mutation effect on KRAS dependency is +0.014 signed, CI [-0.004,0.031]. It remains unresolved and active because KRAS co-mutation contexts may modify the effect. H2 rejects the specific hypothesis that BRAF V600E strengthens BRAF dependency: the upper end of the signed interval is only +0.012, which is not clinically meaningful on the BRFScore scale, and the point estimate is near zero. H4, H5, and H9 remain unresolved/deferred because their intervals are wide or centered near zero; they are not compelling enough for immediate follow-up, but I do not close them as definitive nulls. H10, H11, and H12 are rejected as meaningful directional claims: the intervals are near zero, and the clinically meaningful portion of the intervals is either absent or in the opposite direction (for H12, the expected stronger STAT3 dependency is essentially excluded). I am treating research marker/signature variables cautiously; they are not used as biological evidence here because their assigned roles are absent, and I am not claiming causality or generalizability from these associations alone.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: I corrected the prior proposal by using the public schema variable stk11_loss instead of the misspelled name. These proposals are designed to do two things: refine the already accepted dataset associations and add mechanistically motivated follow-ups for outcomes that have not yet shown convincing context effects. First, I test whether the large SMARCA4-loss effect on SMARCA2 dependency is modified by TP53 loss or additional SWI/SNF-complex injury through ARID1A loss. If SMARCA2 dependency is driven mainly by SMARCA4 paralog loss, these interactions could be absent or modest; if co-losses compound chromatin-complex stress, signed effects in the direction of stronger SMARCA2 dependency would be favored. Second, I test whether the accepted MSI-high effect on WRN dependency and the accepted KEAP1-loss effect on weaker NFE2L2 dependency vary by subtype or KEAP1-adjacent biology. The NFE2L2 interaction with lineage_subtype asks whether the reversed KEAP1 effect is subtype-masked; the interaction with stk11_loss tests whether STK11 co-loss deepens the weaker-dependency signal. STK11 loss is also tested as a standalone predictor of NFE2L2 dependency; if it tracks KEAP1-loss biology, the raw contrast should be positive, i.e., less negative NFE2L2 scores and therefore weaker dependency. Third, I added broader mechanistic hypotheses: BRCA2 loss with DHX9 dependency because homologous-recombination defects may increase dependence on helicase or stress-response machinery; RB1 loss with POLR2A and KIF18A dependency because E2F-driven transcription and cell-cycle activation may increase reliance on transcription and mitotic regulators; PTEN loss with STAT3 dependency because PI3K/AKT and STAT3 survival pathways may intersect; and ERBB2 amplification with both ERBB2 and TMED10 dependency because receptor amplification and trafficking biology may create context-dependent vulnerabilities. ERBB2 amplification was near null for ERBB2 dependency overall, so the adenocarcinoma interaction is specifically a masked-subtype test. All proposed effects remain interpreted as associations within the supplied dataset, not as causal or broadly generalizable claims. I will judge acceptance by absolute dependency-score differences and interval bounds, because relative percent is hard to interpret when mean dependency scores are near zero.

record.narrative:
The new 12-claim panel gives one large new association and several mostly negative or imprecise context/mechanistic follow-ups. I interpreted estimates exactly as signed to the registered direction, so a positive estimate supports the claimed direction and a negative estimate contradicts it.

H41 is the key new finding: PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency, direction -1 (stronger STAT3 dependency), has signed mean_difference +0.267, 95% CI [0.215,0.319]. Because the raw contrast is negative under direction -1, PTEN-loss samples show markedly more negative STAT3 dependency than PTEN-intact samples. This effect is far larger than a 10%-scale threshold for STAT3 scores (the STAT3 mean is about -0.28, so a 10% absolute change is roughly 0.028) and is also large relative to the STAT3 score SD. The interval is well away from zero and includes only clinically meaningful values. I accept H41 as an association in this supplied dataset and request independent validation because it is a strong new association where validation could materially strengthen or constrain the conclusion. I do not interpret PTEN loss as causally inducing STAT3 dependency; co-occurring PI3K/pathway alterations, lineage context, or screen artifacts could contribute, so I registered PTEN-STAT3 context tests.

H20, H21, and H32 reject the proposed modifiers of the accepted SMARCA4-loss effect on SMARCA2 dependency. H20 tested adenocarcinoma subtype interaction: signed estimate -0.028, CI [-0.076,0.020]. H32 tested TP53-loss co-loss interaction: signed estimate -0.015, CI [-0.064,0.035]. Both intervals are centered near or opposite the claimed direction and do not support a clinically meaningful positive interaction; they are tiny relative to the accepted SMARCA4 main effect of +0.784. H21 tested ARID1A loss as an independent SWI/SNF-complex predictor of SMARCA2 dependency: signed estimate -0.017, CI [-0.057,0.023]. It is near zero and does not support stronger SMARCA2 dependency under ARID1A loss. These results do not threaten H6; rather, they suggest that the SMARCA2 dependency association is specific to SMARCA4 loss in this dataset and not broadly explained by adenocarcinoma subtype, TP53 co-loss, or ARID1A loss.

H34, H36, and H37 test whether the accepted MSI-high/WRN and KEAP1/NFE2L2 associations have useful STK11 or lineage context. H34 MSI-high adenocarcinoma interaction is signed -0.021, CI [-0.085,0.042]; H36 KEAP1-by-STK11 interaction is signed -0.026, CI [-0.079,0.026]; H37 STK11 loss main effect on NFE2L2 is signed -0.007, CI [-0.046,0.033]. All are small relative to their accepted main effects and do not provide evidence for the claimed context modifications. However, some intervals include modest positive effects, so I record them as unresolved but deferred rather than as fully closed nulls. The practical conclusion is that these context refinements are low priority compared with H41 and H39.

H22, H23, H38, and H40 are imprecise and not strong enough to accept. H22 EGFR amplification in KRAS-wild-type samples is signed +0.016, CI [-0.014,0.046]. H23 KRAS mutation in TP53-wild-type samples is signed +0.017, CI [-0.003,0.036]. H38 BRCA2 loss versus DHX9 dependency is signed +0.012, CI [-0.020,0.044]. H40 RB1 loss versus KIF18A dependency is signed +0.008, CI [-0.019,0.036]. These estimates are around or below a 10% absolute-scale threshold and have intervals including the null. I do not accept them; because their upper bounds include some clinically meaningful positive effects, I leave them unresolved but deferred unless future evidence or validation makes them informative.

H39 RB1 loss versus POLR2A dependency is borderline: signed +0.025, CI [-0.0009,0.0507]. The point estimate is almost exactly at a roughly 10% absolute-scale threshold for POLR2A dependency, and the interval includes both the null and meaningfully larger positive effects. This is not enough to accept, but it is the most plausible remaining non-PTEN signal from this round, so I keep it active for possible validation or targeted follow-up. H40, using the same RB1 predictor but with KIF18A dependency, is much weaker and remains deferred.

Overall, the strongest supported dataset findings after this round are H6 SMARCA4 loss associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, H7 MSI-high associated with stronger WRN dependency, H13 KEAP1 loss associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and now H41 PTEN loss associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. All are associations in the supplied dataset only. The requested validation for H41 will be assessed when it arrives.

results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

record.narrative: The newly delivered independent validation for H41 decisively supports the PTEN-loss association with stronger STAT3 dependency in this dataset. Because estimates are already signed to the registered direction (-1, i.e., stronger STAT3 dependency), the discovery contrast was +0.267, 95% CI [0.215,0.319], and the independent validation contrast was +0.268 with a stringent independent interval [0.188,0.348]. Both point estimates are almost identical, and the validation lower bound remains far above zero and far above any plausible 10%-scale threshold for the STAT3 score distribution. In raw terms, PTEN-loss lines show substantially more negative STAT3 dependency scores, and this difference is large relative to the STAT3 mean and SD. I therefore accept H41 as a scientifically meaningful dataset association and close direct follow-up on the main effect. This remains an association, not causal evidence or a clinical generalizability claim. I keep H3 unresolved but deferred because its independent validation point estimate was near zero and imprecise, with the interval still spanning both the null and potentially meaningful effects; it is not compelling enough for further immediate validation. The next analyses should focus on registered context tests around the accepted effects, especially H44-H46 for whether the PTEN-STAT3 effect is modified by lineage subtype or PIK3CA biology, H47 for RB1-POLR2A subtype context, and the broad untested coverage claims H14-H19 and H24-H31. If PTEN-STAT3 context interactions are near null, the accepted effect appears stable across these measured contexts; if they are large, they should be followed up cautiously without causal interpretation.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.

Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation

If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Do not infer causality or clinical generalizability from these associations.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"I corrected the prior proposal by using the public schema variable stk11_loss instead of the misspelled name. These proposals are designed to do two things: refine the already accepted dataset associations and add mechanistically motivated follow-ups for outcomes that have not yet shown convincing context effects. First, I test whether the large SMARCA4-loss effect on SMARCA2 dependency is modified by TP53 loss or additional SWI/SNF-complex injury through ARID1A loss. If SMARCA2 dependency is driven mainly by SMARCA4 paralog loss, these interactions could be absent or modest; if co-losses compound chromatin-complex stress, signed effects in the direction of stronger SMARCA2 dependency would be favored. Second, I test whether the accepted MSI-high effect on WRN dependency and the accepted KEAP1-loss effect on weaker NFE2L2 dependency vary by subtype or KEAP1-adjacent biology. The NFE2L2 interaction with lineage_subtype asks whether the reversed KEAP1 effect is subtype-masked; the interaction with stk11_loss tests whether STK11 co-loss deepens the weaker-dependency signal. STK11 loss is also tested as a standalone predictor of NFE2L2 dependency; if it tracks KEAP1-loss biology, the raw contrast should be positive, i.e., less negative NFE2L2 scores and therefore weaker dependency. Third, I added broader mechanistic hypotheses: BRCA2 loss with DHX9 dependency because homologous-recombination defects may increase dependence on helicase or stress-response machinery; RB1 loss with POLR2A and KIF18A dependency because E2F-driven transcription and cell-cycle activation may increase reliance on transcription and mitotic regulators; PTEN loss with STAT3 dependency because PI3K/AKT and STAT3 survival pathways may intersect; and ERBB2 amplification with both ERBB2 and TMED10 dependency because receptor amplification and trafficking biology may create context-dependent vulnerabilities. ERBB2 amplification was near null for ERBB2 dependency overall, so the adenocarcinoma interaction is specifically a masked-subtype test. All proposed effects remain interpreted as associations within the supplied dataset, not as causal or broadly generalizable claims. I will judge acceptance by absolute dependency-score differences and interval bounds, because relative percent is hard to interpret when mean dependency scores are near zero.","analyze":"I selected 12 untested claims that jointly test the robustness of the already accepted dataset associations, refine unresolved mechanistic hypotheses, and broaden coverage of the remaining dependency outcomes. H34 tests whether the accepted MSI-high -> WRN-dependency association differs by lineage subtype. H36 and H37 test STK11 loss as a KEAP1-adjacent biological context and a standalone predictor for the reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 finding. H22 and H23 test EGFR amplification among KRAS-wild-type samples and KRAS mutation among TP53-wild-type samples, respectively, because these cleaner co-mutation strata may resolve the unresolved overall EGFR and KRAS associations. Finally, H38 through H41 test mechanistically motivated binary predictors for underexplored outcomes: BRCA2 loss with DHX9 dependency, RB1 loss with POLR2A and KIF18A dependency, and PTEN loss with STAT3 dependency. This set avoids duplicating existing evidence, maintains adequate expected cell counts, and allocates the next analysis round toward both accepted-effect context and promising new associations. I interpreted estimates exactly as signed to the registered direction, so a positive estimate supports the claimed direction and a negative estimate contradicts it.\n\nH41 is the key new finding: PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency, direction -1 (stronger STAT3 dependency), has signed mean_difference +0.267, 95% CI [0.215,0.319]. Because the raw contrast is negative under direction -1, PTEN-loss samples show markedly more negative STAT3 dependency than PTEN-intact samples. This effect is far larger than a 10%-scale threshold for STAT3 scores (the STAT3 mean is about -0.28, so a 10% absolute change is roughly 0.028) and is also large relative to the STAT3 score SD. The interval is well away from zero and includes only clinically meaningful values. I accept H41 as an association in this supplied dataset and request independent validation because it is a strong new association where validation could materially strengthen or constrain the conclusion. I do not interpret PTEN loss as causally inducing STAT3 dependency; co-occurring PI3K/pathway alterations, lineage context, or screen artifacts could contribute, so I registered PTEN-STAT3 context tests.\n\nH20, H21, and H32 reject the proposed modifiers of the accepted SMARCA4-loss effect on SMARCA2 dependency. H20 tested adenocarcinoma subtype interaction: signed estimate -0.028, CI [-0.076,0.020]. H32 tested TP53-loss co-loss interaction: signed estimate -0.015, CI [-0.064,0.035]. Both intervals are centered near or opposite the claimed direction and do not support a clinically meaningful positive interaction; they are tiny relative to the accepted SMARCA4 main effect of +0.784. H21 tested ARID1A loss as an independent SWI/SNF-complex predictor of SMARCA2 dependency: signed estimate -0.017, CI [-0.057,0.023]. record.narrative: I propose a focused follow-up set after the accepted, largely validated dataset associations. The accepted effects are very large for SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high/WRN dependency, and KEAP1 loss/weaker NFE2L2 dependency, while PTEN loss/stronger STAT3 dependency is now independently validated and large but smaller in absolute terms. The first purpose of these proposals is to test whether the accepted effects survive in biologically relevant, high-frequency subgroups rather than being driven by co-occurring alterations. For PTEN-STAT3, I test PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency among TP53-intact lines. If PTEN loss associated with much more negative STAT3 dependency remains present, the association is less likely to be a mere TP53-co-alteration artifact; if absent, co-TP53 loss could be important. For SMARCA4-SMARCA2, I test among ARID1A-intact lines. Because ARID1A loss alone did not show a meaningful SMARCA2 effect and the ARID1A interaction was not promising, persistence in ARID1A-intact cells would support specificity for SMARCA4 loss. For WRN, I test MSI-high among TP53-intact cells; the accepted MSI effect is enormous, so this is a robustness test against MSI/TP53 co-mutation confounding. For NFE2L2, I test KEAP1 loss among STK11-intact cells because STK11 is a KEAP1-adjacent lung biology context and a prior STK11 interaction was small and inconclusive. The signed direction remains +1 because more positive NFE2L2 dependency scores mean weaker dependency, which was the accepted KEAP1-loss direction. Second, I test whether MYC amplification modifies the accepted SMARCA4-SMARCA2 effect. MYC-driven transcriptional and replication stress could compound chromatin-complex stress and make SMARCA2 dependency more extreme in MYC-amplified cells, but paralog specificity and co-alteration structure may make this absent; the interaction direction is registered as stronger dependency in MYC-amplified versus non-amplified cells, with uncertainty anticipated. Third, I add mechanistic main effects for underresolved outcomes. MYC amplification may increase p53-pathway stress and hence MDM2 dependency in TP53-compatible contexts, so I test stronger MDM2 dependency under MYC amplification, registered direction -1 for more negative scores. NF1 loss de-represses RAS signaling and could increase KRAS dependency even when KRAS mutation status is not directly tested; I register stronger KRAS dependency under NF1 loss, also direction -1. Fourth, I test whether unresolved receptor-tyrosine-kinase and transcription dependencies appear in cleaner co-mutation strata: ERBB2 amplification among KRAS-wild-type cells, because KRAS-mutant bypass signaling could mask ERBB2-amplification effects; RB1 loss among TP53-intact cells for POLR2A, because the overall RB1-POLR2A signal is borderline and p53-loss co-alteration could confound it; and BRAF V600E among KRAS-wild-type cells, because mutual exclusivity with KRAS mutation could make the small overall BRAF contrast uninformative. In each raw expected direction, negative means the exposed group has more negative dependency scores, hence stronger dependency, except for NFE2L2 where positive means exposed scores are less negative, hence weaker dependency. These are hypothesis refinements and broad follow-ups within the supplied lung line dataset only; none should be interpreted as causal or clinically generalizable unless further evidence accumulates.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

comparison cell.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

All conclusions remain dataset associations, not causal or clinical generalizability claims.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"I propose a focused follow-up set after the accepted, largely validated dataset associations. The accepted effects are very large for SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high/WRN dependency, and KEAP1 loss/weaker NFE2L2 dependency, while PTEN loss/stronger STAT3 dependency is now independently validated and large but smaller in absolute terms. The first purpose of these proposals is to test whether the accepted effects survive in biologically relevant, high-frequency subgroups rather than being driven by co-occurring alterations. For PTEN-STAT3, I test PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency among TP53-intact lines. If PTEN loss associated with much more negative STAT3 dependency remains present, the association is less likely to be a mere TP53-co-alteration artifact; if absent, co-TP53 loss could be important. For SMARCA4-SMARCA2, I test among ARID1A-intact lines. Because ARID1A loss alone did not show a meaningful SMARCA2 effect and the ARID1A interaction was not promising, persistence in ARID1A-intact cells would support specificity for SMARCA4 loss. For WRN, I test MSI-high among TP53-intact cells; the accepted MSI effect is enormous, so this is a robustness test against MSI/TP53 co-mutation confounding. For NFE2L2, I test KEAP1 loss among STK11-intact cells because STK11 is a KEAP1-adjacent lung biology context and a prior STK11 interaction was small and inconclusive. The signed direction remains +1 because more positive NFE2L2 dependency scores mean weaker dependency, which was the accepted KEAP1-loss direction. Second, I test whether MYC amplification modifies the accepted SMARCA4-SMARCA2 effect. MYC-driven transcriptional and replication stress could compound chromatin-complex stress and make SMARCA2 dependency more extreme in MYC-amplified cells, but paralog specificity and co-alteration structure may make this absent; the interaction direction is registered as stronger dependency in MYC-amplified versus non-amplified cells, with uncertainty anticipated. Third, I add mechanistic main effects for underresolved outcomes. MYC amplification may increase p53-pathway stress and hence MDM2 dependency in TP53-compatible contexts, so I test stronger MDM2 dependency under MYC amplification, registered direction -1 for more negative scores. NF1 loss de-represses RAS signaling and could increase KRAS dependency even when KRAS mutation status is not directly tested; I register stronger KRAS dependency under NF1 loss, also direction -1. Fourth, I test whether unresolved receptor-tyrosine-kinase and transcription dependencies appear in cleaner co-mutation strata: ERBB2 amplification among KRAS-wild-type cells, because KRAS-mutant bypass signaling could mask ERBB2-amplification effects; RB1 loss among TP53-intact cells for POLR2A, because the overall RB1-POLR2A signal is borderline and p53-loss co-alteration could confound it; and BRAF V600E among KRAS-wild-type cells, because mutual exclusivity with KRAS mutation could make the small overall BRAF contrast uninformative. In each raw expected direction, negative means the exposed group has more negative dependency scores, hence stronger dependency, except for NFE2L2 where positive means exposed scores are less negative, hence weaker dependency. These are hypothesis refinements and broad follow-ups within the supplied lung line dataset only; none should be interpreted as causal or clinically generalizable unless further evidence accumulates.","analyze":"I selected 12 untested claims that jointly test the robustness of the already accepted dataset associations, refine unresolved mechanistic hypotheses, and broaden coverage of the remaining dependency outcomes. H20 and H32 test whether the very large SMARCA4-loss -> SMARCA2-dependency association is modified by adenocarcinoma subtype or TP53 co-loss; H21 tests an independent SWI/SNF-complex predictor, ARID1A loss, for SMARCA2 dependency. H34 tests whether the accepted MSI-high -> WRN-dependency association differs by lineage subtype. H36 and H37 test STK11 loss as a KEAP1-adjacent biological context and a standalone predictor for the reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 finding. H22 and H23 test EGFR amplification among KRAS-wild-type samples and KRAS mutation among TP53-wild-type samples, respectively, because these cleaner co-mutation strata may resolve the unresolved overall EGFR and KRAS associations. Finally, H38 through H41 test mechanistically motivated binary predictors for underexplored outcomes: BRCA2 loss with DHX9 dependency, RB1 loss with POLR2A and KIF18A dependency, and PTEN loss with STAT3 dependency. This set avoids duplicating existing evidence, maintains adequate expected cell counts, and allocates the next analysis round toward both accepted-effect context and promising new associations. All resulting effects will still be interpreted as dataset associations, not causal or generalizable clinical claims.","appraise":"The new 12-claim panel gives one large new association and several mostly negative or imprecise context/mechanistic follow-ups. I interpreted estimates exactly as signed to the registered direction, so a positive estimate supports the claimed direction and a negative estimate contradicts it.\n\nH41 is the key new finding: PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency, direction -1 (stronger STAT3 dependency), has signed mean_difference +0.267, 95% CI [0.215,0.319]. Because the raw contrast is negative under direction -1, PTEN-loss samples show markedly more negative STAT3 dependency than PTEN-intact samples. This effect is far larger than a 10%-scale threshold for STAT3 scores (the STAT3 mean is about -0.28, so a 10% absolute change is roughly 0.028) and is also large relative to the STAT3 score SD. The interval is well away from zero and includes only clinically meaningful values. I accept H41 as an association in this supplied dataset and request independent validation because it is a strong new association where validation could materially strengthen or constrain the conclusion. record.narrative:
I interpreted every signed estimate as reported: a positive signed value supports the registered hypothesis direction, while a negative signed value contradicts it. The strongest new evidence confirms that the accepted main-effect associations are not confined to the full sample and do not appear to be simple artifacts of the most obvious co-alteration contexts. H48, PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency among TP53-intact lines, has signed mean_difference +0.287, 95% CI [0.227,0.347]. This is far larger than an approximate 10% scale change for the STAT3 score distribution and far away from zero, so I accept it and close direct follow-up. H46, PTEN loss among PIK3CA-intact lines, is similarly large: +0.267, CI [0.210,0.323]. Together with H48, this strongly suggests that the accepted PTEN-loss association with stronger STAT3 dependency is not explained only by TP53 co-loss or PIK3CA-mutant context, although co-alteration structure and technical confounding remain possible. H49, SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-intact lines, remains enormous: +0.777, CI [0.756,0.798], supporting specificity of the SMARCA4-loss association for SMARCA2 dependency rather than a broad SWI/SNF effect, because ARID1A loss alone was not supported. H50, MSI-high among TP53-intact lines, remains enormous: +0.780, CI [0.747,0.813], so the MSI-high WRN association is robust to TP53 co-loss in this dataset. H51, KEAP1 loss among STK11-intact lines, is +0.801, CI [0.779,0.823], reinforcing the accepted reversed NFE2L2 direction: KEAP1 loss is associated with less negative, hence weaker, NFE2L2 dependency. For NFE2L2 the mean score is close to zero, so a 10% relative threshold is not the best guide, but the absolute interval is very large relative to the score SD and is not compatible with a trivial effect.

The modifier tests are less informative. H44, adenocarcinoma interaction for PTEN-STAT3, is centered near zero, +0.001, CI [-0.115,0.117]. This provides no evidence that the PTEN effect is stronger in adenocarcinoma than in other subtypes, but the interval is wide and includes clinically meaningful positive effects, so I record it as unresolved and deferred rather than accepting a null conclusion. H52, MYC amplification interaction for SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency, is +0.035, CI [-0.024,0.094]; it is small relative to the main SMARCA4 effect and underpowered in MYC-amplified cells. It does not support a meaningful MYC-specific modification enough to accept, but the upper bound prevents a hard rejection. H53, MYC amplification versus stronger MDM2 dependency, is +0.008, CI [-0.020,0.036]. The point estimate is small and near null; the upper bound just touches a plausible clinical threshold, so I leave it unresolved but deferred rather than treating it as a promising new association.

The remaining mechanistic or co-mutation refinement tests mostly do not support the registered directions. H54, NF1 loss versus stronger KRAS dependency, is signed -0.020, CI [-0.049,0.009], contradicting the claimed stronger-dependency direction. H55, ERBB2 amplification among KRAS-wild-type lines, is signed -0.009, CI [-0.042,0.024], also inconsistent with the claimed direction and not clinically meaningful. H57, BRAF V600E among KRAS-wild-type lines, is signed -0.019, CI [-0.051,0.013], similarly inconsistent with the claimed stronger BRAF dependency. I reject H54, H55, and H57 as supported claims for the registered directions and close them. H56, RB1 loss among TP53-intact lines for POLR2A dependency, is +0.016, CI [-0.013,0.045]. It is close to a 10% absolute-scale threshold and imprecise, and it mirrors the borderline overall H39 signal. I leave H56 unresolved but deferred.

Overall, the new evidence materially strengthens confidence in the accepted dataset associations by showing robustness in common biological strata: PTEN-STAT3 survives TP53-intact and PIK3CA-intact contexts; SMARCA4-SMARCA2 survives ARID1A-intact context; MSI-high-WRN survives TP53-intact context; and KEAP1-NFE2L2 survives STK11-intact context. The most useful unresolved candidate is RB1 loss for POLR2A dependency, especially H39, because both the overall estimate and H56 are near a threshold and imprecise. I therefore request independent validation of H39. I also registered batch-robustness proposals for the strongest accepted associations because screen batch could contribute to dependencies or to predictor distribution; if these effects persist within batch_a, technical batch confounding becomes less plausible, although this still would remain a dataset association and not a causal or generalizable claim.

record.narrative:
All estimates were interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so a positive value supports the registered claim and a negative value contradicts it. The new validation evidence resolves several important priorities. H7, MSI-high versus WRN dependency, is now independently supported. The discovery signed contrast was +0.790, 95% CI [0.760,0.819], and the independent validation signed contrast was +0.812 with a stringent interval [0.765,0.858]. The two point estimates are nearly identical, and the validation lower bound is far above zero and far above a practical 10%-scale change for WRN scores. In raw terms, MSI-high lines have markedly more negative WRN dependency scores, indicating stronger WRN dependency. I therefore accept H7 as a scientifically meaningful association in this supplied dataset and close direct follow-up on the main effect. This remains an association, not causal evidence or a generalizable clinical claim.

The response deadline for H3 requires reassessing the EGFR-amplification main effect. The discovery evidence was borderline and not decisive: signed +0.025, CI [-0.0003,0.0507]. The independent validation is near null: signed +0.0015, CI [-0.043,0.046]. The validation point estimate is far below a clinically meaningful scale for EGFR dependency, and it does not replicate the discovery signal. However, the validation interval still includes both positive values around the 10% threshold and negative values, so this is not a definitive exclusion of a moderate effect. Because the claim was never accepted and the validation does not provide support, I leave H3 unresolved but close further investigation rather than spend more resources on a failed replication candidate. This is not evidence that EGFR amplification is irrelevant in all contexts; it is evidence that this supplied dataset does not support a meaningful accepted association for the registered direction.

H39, RB1 loss versus POLR2A dependency, shows the same pattern after its validation request. Discovery was borderline positive, signed +0.0249, CI [-0.0009,0.0507], but independent validation is essentially centered at zero: signed +0.00019, CI [-0.0384,0.0388]. The validation fails to support the proposed stronger POLR2A dependency under RB1 loss. The interval remains wide enough to include clinically meaningful positive and negative values, so I do not claim a precise null. I therefore leave H39 unresolved but close the main-effect investigation because the validation does not justify acceptance or further targeted follow-up. Related stratum tests such as H56 and H47 remain low priority for the same reason.

The first proposed block tests whether the accepted effects persist within the dominant Avana CRISPR library. Library choice can affect guide performance and apparent dependency scores, so if the SMARCA4-SMARCA2, MSI-WRN, KEAP1-NFE2L2, and PTEN-STAT3 contrasts remain large within crispr_library_avana=1, library-specific technical confounding becomes less plausible. MYC amplification can increase p53-pathway stress and may make MDM2 or USP7 dependency stronger primarily when p53 is intact; the proposed TP53-intact strata test whether the near-null or unresolved full-sample MYC associations concentrate in biologically coherent lines. Plausible alternatives include p53-independent MYC effects, co-alteration structure, or true absence of MYC specificity. BRCA2 loss could increase WRN dependency through homologous-recombination and replication-stress conflicts, and MSI-high could increase DHX9 dependency because microsatellite instability creates replication and DNA repair stress. If these stratum-specific effects remain large and positive as signed, the validated PTEN-STAT3 association is not simply dependent on TP53 loss, PIK3CA mutation, or lineage subtype. H49 and H52 test the accepted SMARCA4-loss association with SMARCA2 dependency: H49 tests SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-intact lines to test paralog/SWI-SNF specificity, and H52 tests whether MYC amplification modifies SMARCA2 dependency under SMARCA4 loss. H50 tests MSI-high versus WRN dependency among TP53-intact lines to assess whether the huge MSI-high signal survives a common co-mutation context. H51 tests KEAP1 loss versus NFE2L2 dependency among STK11-intact lines, addressing the reversed accepted direction and STK11-adjacent biology. H53 and H54 test new mechanistic main effects for outcomes with limited context evidence: MYC amplification as a predictor of stronger MDM2 dependency, and NF1 loss as a predictor of stronger KRAS dependency. H55 and H56 refine borderline/unresolved associations in cleaner co-mutation strata: ERBB2 amplification among KRAS-wild-type lines for ERBB2 dependency, and RB1 loss among TP53-intact lines for POLR2A dependency. record.narrative: I selected twelve previously registered but untested comparisons to maximize the value of this batch of analyses. The first four are library-robustness tests for the strongest accepted associations: H65 tests MSI-high versus WRN dependency within Avana-library screens; H66 tests SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA2 dependency within Avana-library screens; H67 tests KEAP1 loss versus NFE2L2 dependency within Avana-library screens; H68 tests PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency within Avana-library screens. For all four, a positive signed estimate supports the registered direction. If these contrasts remain large and positive in the dominant Avana stratum, library-specific technical confounding becomes less plausible; if a contrast collapses or reverses, the accepted association would need a narrower technical interpretation rather than the broad sample-level interpretation. The next four complete co-mutation context tests for the accepted associations: H69 tests PTEN loss among TP53-loss lines, complementing the accepted TP53-intact stratum; H70 tests PTEN loss among PIK3CA-mutant lines, complementing the accepted PIK3CA-intact stratum; H71 tests KEAP1 loss among STK11-loss lines, complementing the accepted STK11-intact stratum; H72 tests SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-loss lines, complementing the accepted ARID1A-intact stratum. These tests ask whether accepted effects are broad across common co-alteration contexts or restricted to specific p53, PI3K, STK11, or ARID1A backgrounds. The remaining four add focused mechanistic coverage for outcomes where current accepted predictors are incomplete: H73 tests whether MYC amplification is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in TP53-intact lines, and H74 tests whether MYC amplification is associated with stronger USP7 dependency in TP53-intact lines; both register direction -1, so positive signed estimates indicate more negative dependency scores and stronger dependency. H75 tests BRCA2 loss as a predictor of stronger WRN dependency, and H76 tests MSI-high as a predictor of stronger DHX9 dependency. These are not yet supported and may be null, but they test plausible replication-stress relationships and expand predictor coverage. I chose library robustness over the earlier batch_a claims because Avana comprises a much larger stratum and gives more precise technical robustness estimates; batch_a claims can remain deferred unless the library tests indicate technical context dependence.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not

Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

All interpretations are associations within the supplied lung CRISPR dataset only, not causal or clinically generalizable.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The strongest current claims are dataset associations, not causal claims: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. For all signed proposals below, a positive signed estimate supports the registered direction; for outcomes where direction -1 was registered, that means the exposed group has more negative dependency scores and therefore stronger dependency. For NFE2L2, direction +1 was registered because KEAP1 loss was associated with less negative, i.e. weaker, NFE2L2 dependency.  The first proposed block tests whether the accepted effects persist within the dominant Avana CRISPR library. Library choice can affect guide performance and apparent dependency scores, so if the SMARCA4-SMARCA2, MSI-WRN, KEAP1-NFE2L2, and PTEN-STAT3 contrasts remain large within crispr_library_avana=1, library-specific technical confounding becomes less plausible. If they collapse in that stratum, the accepted main effects would need a narrower technical interpretation. The second block tests co-mutation contexts that are complementary to accepted strata. For PTEN-STAT3, H48 accepted the TP53-intact context and H46 accepted the PIK3CA-intact context; I now propose direct comparisons among TP53-loss lines and PIK3CA-mutant lines to determine whether the accepted effect is only present in p53-intact or PIK3CA-intact lines. For KEAP1-NFE2L2, H51 accepted the STK11-intact context; the proposed STK11-loss stratum tests whether the reversed NFE2L2 direction is also broad across common KEAP1 co-alterations. For SMARCA4-SMARCA2, H49 accepted the ARID1A-intact context; the proposed ARID1A-loss stratum tests whether SMARCA4-loss specificity survives when ARID1A is also lost. The third block is mechanistic p53-pathway refinement. MYC amplification can increase p53-pathway stress and may make MDM2 or USP7 dependency stronger primarily when p53 is intact; the proposed TP53-intact strata test whether the near-null or unresolved full-sample MYC associations concentrate in biologically coherent lines. Plausible alternatives include p53-independent MYC effects, co-alteration structure, or true absence of MYC specificity. The fourth block adds broad replication-stress hypotheses for underresolved dependencies. BRCA2 loss could increase WRN dependency through homologous-recombination and replication-stress conflicts, and MSI-high could increase DHX9 dependency because microsatellite instability creates replication and DNA repair stress. These are plausible but not established in the ledger, and effects may be absent or small. They are useful coverage for WRN and DHX9 outside the accepted predictor set. I deliberately avoid further EGFR-amplification and RB1-loss follow-up because those candidates did not replicate well and remain low-priority. All proposals remain association tests within the supplied lung CRISPR dataset only; they do not establish causality or clinical generalizability.","analyze":"I selected twelve previously registered but untested comparisons to maximize the value of this batch of analyses. The first four are library-robustness tests for the strongest accepted associations: H65 tests MSI-high versus WRN dependency within Avana-library screens; H66 tests SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA2 dependency within Avana-library screens; H67 tests KEAP1 loss versus NFE2L2 dependency within Avana-library screens; H68 tests PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency within Avana-library screens. For all four, a positive signed estimate supports the registered direction. If these contrasts remain large and positive in the dominant Avana stratum, library-specific technical confounding becomes less plausible; if a contrast collapses or reverses, the accepted association would need a narrower technical interpretation rather than the broad sample-level interpretation. The next four complete co-mutation context tests for the accepted associations: H69 tests PTEN loss among TP53-loss lines, complementing the accepted TP53-intact stratum; H70 tests PTEN loss among PIK3CA-mutant lines, complementing the accepted PIK3CA-intact stratum; H71 tests KEAP1 loss among STK11-loss lines, complementing the accepted STK11-intact stratum; H72 tests SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-loss lines, complementing the accepted ARID1A-intact stratum. These tests ask whether accepted effects are broad across common co-alteration contexts or restricted to specific p53, PI3K, STK11, or ARID1A backgrounds. The remaining four add focused mechanistic coverage for outcomes where current accepted predictors are incomplete: H73 tests whether MYC amplification is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in TP53-intact lines, and H74 tests whether MYC amplification is associated with stronger USP7 dependency in TP53-intact lines; both register direction -1, so positive signed estimates indicate more negative dependency scores and stronger dependency. H75 tests BRCA2 loss as a predictor of stronger WRN dependency, and H76 tests MSI-high as a predictor of stronger DHX9 dependency. These are not yet supported and may be null, but they test plausible replication-stress relationships and expand predictor coverage. I chose library robustness over the earlier batch_a claims because Avana comprises a much larger stratum and gives more precise technical robustness estimates; batch_a claims can remain deferred unless the library tests indicate technical context dependence.","appraise":"I interpreted every signed estimate as reported: a positive signed value supports the registered hypothesis direction, while a negative signed value contradicts it. The strongest new evidence confirms that the accepted main-effect associations are not confined to the full sample and do not appear to be simple artifacts of the most obvious co-alteration contexts. H48, PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency among TP53-intact lines, has signed mean_difference +0.287, 95% CI [0.227,0.347]. This is far larger than an approximate 10% scale change for the STAT3 score distribution and far away from zero, so I accept it and close direct follow-up. H46, PTEN loss among PIK3CA-intact lines, is similarly large: +0.267, CI [0.210,0.323]. Together with H48, this strongly suggests that the accepted PTEN-loss association with stronger STAT3 dependency is not explained only by TP53 co-loss or PIK3CA-mutant context, although co-alteration structure and technical confounding remain possible. H49, SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-intact lines, remains enormous: +0.777, CI [0.756,0.798], supporting specificity of the SMARCA4-loss association for SMARCA2 dependency rather than a broad SWI/SNF effect, because ARID1A loss alone was not supported. H50, MSI-high among TP53-intact lines, remains enormous: +0.780, CI [0.747,0.813], so the MSI-high WRN association is robust to TP53 co-loss in this dataset. H51, KEAP1 loss among STK11-intact lines, is +0.801, CI [0.779,0.823], reinforcing the accepted reversed NFE2L2 direction: KEAP1 loss is associated with less negative, hence weaker, NFE2L2 dependency. For NFE2L2 the mean score is close to zero, so a 10% relative threshold is not the best guide, but the absolute interval is very large relative to the score SD and is not compatible with a trivial effect.\n\nThe modifier tests are less informative. H44, adenocarcinoma interaction for PTEN-STAT3, is centered near zero, +0.001, CI [-0.115,0.117]. This provides no evidence that the PTEN effect is stronger in adenocarcinoma than in other subtypes, but the interval is wide and includes clinically meaningful positive effects, so I record it as unresolved and deferred rather than accepting a null conclusion. H52, MYC amplification interaction for SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency, is +0.035, CI [-0.024,0.094]; it is small relative to the main SMARCA4 effect and underpowered in MYC-amplified cells. It does not support a meaningful MYC-specific modification enough to accept, but the upper bound prevents a hard rejection. H53, MYC amplification versus stronger MDM2 dependency, is +0.008, CI [-0.020,0.036]. The point estimate is small and near null; the upper bound just touches a plausible clinical threshold, so I leave it unresolved but deferred rather than treating it as a promising new association.\n\nThe remaining mechanistic or co-mutation refinement tests mostly do not support the registered directions.
