record.narrative:
All new estimates were interpreted as already signed to the registered direction, so positive values support the hypothesis and negative values contradict it. For outcomes where direction -1 was registered, a positive signed estimate means more negative dependency scores in the exposed group and therefore stronger dependency. For H67, direction +1 means KEAP1 loss is associated with less negative, hence weaker, NFE2L2 dependency.

The four Avana-library robustness tests are all highly consistent with the corresponding main accepted effects. H65 tests MSI-high versus WRN dependency among Avana screens: signed estimate +0.794, 95% CI [0.764,0.825]. This is essentially the same enormous positive contrast as the main MSI-high effect and is far above zero and far above any plausible scale of trivial change for WRN scores. I accept H65 and close it. H66 tests SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA2 dependency among Avana screens: +0.781, CI [0.760,0.802]. This remains enormous relative to the SMARCA2 score distribution and supports the accepted SMARCA4-SMARCA2 association inside the dominant library. I accept and close it. H67 tests KEAP1 loss versus NFE2L2 dependency among Avana screens in the accepted reversed direction: +0.796, CI [0.774,0.818]. This is again very large and supports KEAP1 loss being associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. I accept and close it. H68 tests PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency among Avana screens: +0.288, CI [0.232,0.343]. This is comparable to the main and validated PTEN-STAT3 effect, so library-specific technical confounding becomes much less plausible. I accept and close H68.

The co-mutation context tests also support broad robustness of the strongest accepted associations. H69 tests PTEN loss among TP53-loss lines: +0.190, CI [0.085,0.296]. The interval is entirely positive and the point estimate is large relative to the STAT3 score scale; even the lower bound represents a practically meaningful absolute shift for STAT3 dependency. Although the TP53-loss sample is smaller than the TP53-intact stratum, the evidence is sufficient to accept the PTEN-STAT3 association in this complementary context. I accept and close H69. H70 tests PTEN loss among PIK3CA-mutant lines: +0.268, CI [0.127,0.409]. The estimate is large, the interval excludes zero, and the lower bound is still substantial, but the exposed cell size is only 38, so uncertainty is wide. I accept this cautiously and close further direct testing, interpreting it as a stratum-specific association rather than precise generalizability. H71 tests KEAP1 loss among STK11-loss lines: +0.775, CI [0.727,0.823]. This is huge and consistent with the accepted reversed NFE2L2 direction, so KEAP1 loss appears associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency irrespective of STK11 co-loss. I accept and close H71. H72 tests SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-loss lines: +0.814, CI [0.767,0.862]. This is larger than the ARID1A-intact stratum and supports the claim that the SMARCA4-loss effect is not driven merely by ARID1A status. I accept and close H72.

The mechanistic MYC and replication-stress tests do not support the registered directions enough to accept. H73 tests MYC amplification versus stronger MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact lines: +0.008, CI [-0.023,0.040]. This is essentially null. The interval includes both trivial and modest effects, but the point estimate is not clinically meaningful and there is no basis for acceptance. I leave it unresolved but close further follow-up because it is now a low-priority candidate. H74 tests MYC amplification versus stronger USP7 dependency among TP53-intact lines: +0.018, CI [-0.007,0.043]. This is small, imprecise, and not convincing; the full-sample USP7-MYC candidate was already weak. I leave it unresolved and close direct follow-up.

H75 tests BRCA2 loss versus stronger WRN dependency: signed estimate approximately zero, -0.00008, CI [-0.045,0.045]. Despite n=130 exposed, the estimate is near null and the interval is wide. This does not support a biologically meaningful BRCA2-WRN association in this dataset, but the interval is too imprecise to claim a precise null. I leave it unresolved and close it because it is not a promising priority. H76 tests MSI-high versus stronger DHX9 dependency: +0.017, CI [-0.017,0.052]. The point estimate is small relative to the DHX9 score distribution and the interval includes zero. Unlike the huge MSI-high-WRN effect, MSI-high does not appear to predict DHX9 dependency in this dataset. I leave H76 unresolved and close further follow-up.

Methodologically, the new stratum tests meet the minimum cell-size rule, but some accepted co-mutation strata are smaller and therefore less precise, especially H70. The large accepted effects are so far from zero that they remain compelling despite multiplicity and subgroup testing. The library robustness tests reduce, but do not eliminate, concern that CRISPR library choice contributes to apparent dependency differences. These are still associations in the supplied dataset, not causal or clinically generalizable claims. To strengthen the accepted set, I request independent validation of H6, the main SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA2-dependency association, because it is central to the current findings and one of the accepted main effects not yet independently validated.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.

use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

This is essentially the same enormous positive contrast as the main MSI-high effect and is far above zero and far above any plausible scale of trivial change for WRN scores. I accept H65 and close it. H66 tests SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA2 dependency among Avana screens: +0.781, CI [0.760,0.802]. This remains enormous relative to the SMARCA2 score distribution and supports the accepted SMARCA4-SMARCA2 association inside the dominant library. I accept and close it. H67 tests KEAP1 loss versus NFE2L2 dependency among Avana screens in the accepted reversed direction: +0.796, CI [0.774,0.818]. This is again very large and supports KEAP1 loss being associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. I accept and close it. H68 tests PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency among Avana screens: +0.288, CI [0.232,0.343]. This is comparable to the main and validated PTEN-STAT3 effect, so library-specific technical confounding becomes much less plausible. I accept and close H68.\n\nThe co-mutation context tests also support broad robustness of the strongest accepted associations. H69 tests PTEN loss among TP53-loss lines: +0.190, CI [0.085,0.296]. The interval is entirely positive and the point estimate is large relative to the STAT3 score scale; even the lower bound represents a practically meaningful absolute shift for STAT3 dependency. Although the TP53-loss sample is smaller than the TP53-intact stratum, the evidence is sufficient to accept the PTEN-STAT3 association in this complementary context. I accept and close H69. H70 tests PTEN loss among PIK3CA-mutant lines: +0.268, CI [0.127,0.409]. The estimate is large, the interval excludes zero, and the lower bound is still substantial, but the exposed cell size is only 38, so uncertainty is wide. record.narrative: All estimates were interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For claims with direction -1, a positive signed estimate corresponds to a more negative raw dependency score in the exposed group and therefore stronger dependency. For H41, this means PTEN-loss lines have stronger STAT3 dependency. For H6, this means SMARCA4-loss lines have stronger SMARCA2 dependency. The new validation evidence supports the main SMARCA4-loss effect very strongly. The discovery contrast for H6 was +0.784, 95% CI [0.765, 0.803], and the independent validation was +0.804, independent 95% interval [0.775, 0.833]. The two point estimates are almost identical, both cell sizes are large in validation, and the validation lower bound is extremely far above zero and far above any plausible 10%-scale practical threshold on the SMARCA2 dependency scale. The SMARCA2 outcome has mean approximately -0.415 and SD approximately 0.366, so an effect near +0.8 signed corresponds to a very large shift toward more negative scores. I therefore accept H6 as a scientifically meaningful dataset association and close the main-effect investigation. This remains an association within the supplied lung CRISPR dataset, not causal or clinical evidence. The H41 response deadline reassesses PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency. The discovery signed contrast was +0.267, CI [0.215, 0.319], and independent validation was +0.268, independent interval [0.188, 0.348]. The validation estimate replicates the discovery estimate almost exactly, the stringent interval excludes zero, and even the lower bound is large relative to the STAT3 score SD of approximately 0.246. I therefore reaffirm H41 as accepted and closed. Overall, the current strongest validated dataset associations are SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and, from discovery and stratum evidence, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The KEAP1-NFE2L2 main claim remains accepted on discovery evidence and is robust in Avana-library, STK11-intact, and STK11-loss strata, but it has not yet had its own independent validation request. Several candidate associations were not supported or failed replication: EGFR amplification versus EGFR dependency did not replicate and is closed unresolved; RB1 loss versus POLR2A dependency was near null in validation and is closed unresolved; BRAF V600E, ARID1A loss, NF1 loss, ERBB2 amplification in KRAS-wild-type context, MYC amplification versus DHX9 or POLR2A, and several MYC/TP53 co-stratum candidates did not support clinically meaningful dependencies in this dataset. The most informative next analyses are subtype and batch robustness checks for the accepted effects: adenocarcinoma-stratum tests H14/H62 for SMARCA2, H15 for WRN, H63 for NFE2L2, and H64 for STAT3, followed by batch_a tests H58-H61 if resources remain. If these remain large and consistent, the accepted associations become less likely to be driven by a single technical or subtype stratum, though still only dataset associations.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.

independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

This is essentially the same enormous positive contrast as the main MSI-high effect and is far above zero and far above any plausible scale of trivial change for WRN scores. I accept H65 and close it. H66 tests SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA2 dependency among Avana screens: +0.781, CI [0.760,0.802]. This remains enormous relative to the SMARCA2 score distribution and supports the accepted SMARCA4-SMARCA2 association inside the dominant library. I accept and close it. Although the TP53-loss sample is smaller than the TP53-intact stratum, the evidence is sufficient to accept the PTEN-STAT3 association in this complementary context. I accept and close H69. H70 tests PTEN loss among PIK3CA-mutant lines: +0.268, CI [0.127,0.409]. The estimate is large, the interval excludes zero, and the lower bound is still substantial, but the exposed cell size is only 38, so uncertainty is wide. I accept this cautiously and close further direct testing, interpreting it as a stratum-specific association rather than precise generalizability. If these contrasts remain large and positive in the dominant Avana stratum, library-specific technical confounding becomes less plausible; if a contrast collapses or reverses, the accepted association would need a narrower technical interpretation rather than the broad sample-level interpretation. The remaining four add focused mechanistic coverage for outcomes where current accepted predictors are incomplete: H73 tests whether MYC amplification is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in TP53-intact lines, and H74 tests whether MYC amplification is associated with stronger USP7 dependency in TP53-intact lines; both register direction -1, so positive signed estimates indicate more negative dependency scores and stronger dependency. This is again very large and supports KEAP1 loss being associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. I accept and close it. H70 tests PTEN loss among PIK3CA-mutant lines: +0.268, CI [0.127,0.409]. The estimate is large, the interval excludes zero, and the lower bound is still substantial, but the exposed cell size is only 38, so uncertainty is wide. I accept this cautiously and close further direct testing, interpreting it as a stratum-specific association rather than precise generalizability. This is huge and consistent with the accepted reversed NFE2L2 direction, so KEAP1 loss appears associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency irrespective of STK11 co-loss. I accept and close H71. To strengthen the accepted set, I request independent validation of H6, the main SMARCA4-loss versus SMARCA2-dependency association, because it is central to the current findings and one of the accepted main effects not yet independently validated.","synthesize":"All estimates were interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For claims with direction -1, a positive signed estimate corresponds to a more negative raw dependency score in the exposed group and therefore stronger dependency. For H41, this means PTEN-loss lines have stronger STAT3 dependency. For H6, this means SMARCA4-loss lines have stronger SMARCA2 dependency. The new validation evidence supports the main SMARCA4-loss effect very strongly. The discovery contrast for H6 was +0.784, 95% CI [0.765, 0.803], and the independent validation was +0.804, independent 95% interval [0.775, 0.833]. The two point estimates are almost identical, both cell sizes are large in validation, and the validation lower bound is extremely far above zero and far above any plausible 10%-scale practical threshold on the SMARCA2 dependency scale. The SMARCA2 outcome has mean approximately -0.415 and SD approximately 0.366, so an effect near +0.8 signed corresponds to a very large shift toward more negative scores. I therefore accept H6 as a scientifically meaningful dataset association and close the main-effect investigation. This remains an association within the supplied lung CRISPR dataset, not causal or clinical evidence. The H41 response deadline reassesses PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency. The discovery signed contrast was +0.267, CI [0.215, 0.319], and independent validation was +0.268, independent interval [0.188, 0.348]. The validation estimate replicates the discovery estimate almost exactly, the stringent interval excludes zero, and even the lower bound is large relative to the STAT3 score SD of approximately 0.246. I therefore reaffirm H41 as accepted and closed. Overall, the current strongest validated dataset associations are SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and, from discovery and stratum evidence, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The KEAP1-NFE2L2 main claim remains accepted on discovery evidence and is robust in Avana-library, STK11-intact, and STK11-loss strata, but it has not yet had its own independent validation request. record.narrative:
All proposed estimates should be interpreted using the registered signed-estimate convention. For claims with direction -1, a positive reported estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative, so the exposed cell has more negative dependency scores and therefore stronger dependency. For claims with direction +1, a positive reported estimate means the exposed cell has less negative scores and therefore weaker dependency. A clinically meaningful result should be large relative to each outcome's score distribution and should have an interval excluding zero with a lower bound beyond a small or trivial shift. These remain association tests in the supplied lung CRISPR dataset only, not causal or clinically generalizable claims.

The first block refines the accepted KEAP1-loss association with weaker NFE2L2 dependency by KRAS-mutation status. KEAP1 loss and KRAS mutation are common in lung adenocarcinoma biology, so if the large reversed effect persists in both KRAS-mutant and KRAS-wildtype strata, the association is less likely to be confined to one driver background. If it collapses or reverses in one stratum, the main effect would need a narrower context interpretation.

The second block refines the accepted SMARCA4-loss association with stronger SMARCA2 dependency by KRAS-mutation status. H6 and related strata are already very large and independently validated, so these KRAS-context tests ask whether the effect is robust across two major oncogenic-driver backgrounds. Plausible alternatives include context dilution, co-alteration confounding, or persistence of a broad chromatin-dependency effect.

The third block refines the accepted PTEN-loss association with stronger STAT3 dependency by KRAS-mutation status. PTEN loss has been robust in TP53-intact, TP53-loss, PIK3CA-intact, PIK3CA-mutant, and Avana-library strata. KRAS-mutant and KRAS-wildtype strata test whether another common driver background modifies the effect.

The fourth block completes the MSI-high-WRN context map in TP53-loss lines. The main MSI-high effect is huge and independently validated, and the TP53-intact stratum is accepted, but the TP53-loss cell is smaller. This is a robustness and cell-size stress test rather than a discovery of a new effect.

The fifth block adds focused mechanistic coverage for RPL11. MYC amplification can increase translational and ribosomal stress, potentially producing stronger RPL11 dependency preferentially when TP53 is intact. The full-sample MYC-RPL11 relationship is not promising enough to prioritize broadly, but the TP53-intact context is a more specific p53-dependent hypothesis.

The last three proposals test pathway-bypass and co-dependency logic around RAS and receptor tyrosine kinase dependencies. PIK3CA mutation may reduce KRAS dependency through downstream PI3K activation, so the registered direction is weaker KRAS dependency. STK11 loss in KRAS-mutant lines may reflect metabolic stress and co-mutational biology, possibly altering KRAS dependency in either direction. KRAS mutation may reduce ERBB2 dependency because mutually exclusive or bypass driver programs can substitute for HER2 signaling. These are exploratory associations; null, small, or reversed results would be acceptable and informative.

I closed or deferred low-priority old active claims related to EGFR amplification, RB1 loss, ERBB2 interactions, redundant ARID1A/PIK3CA interaction tests, and other broad MYC or pathway candidates that have either failed validation, been superseded by stronger stratum evidence, or remain unlikely to yield meaningful differences. This preserves analysis capacity for accepted-effect subtype robustness, KRAS-context robustness, batch_a checks if still desired, and the new focused mechanistic tests.

A clinically meaningful result should be large relative to each outcome's score distribution and should have an interval excluding zero with a lower bound beyond a small or trivial shift. These remain association tests in the supplied lung CRISPR dataset only, not causal or clinically generalizable claims.\n\nThe first block refines the accepted KEAP1-loss association with weaker NFE2L2 dependency by KRAS-mutation status. KEAP1 loss and KRAS mutation are common in lung adenocarcinoma biology, so if the large reversed effect persists in both KRAS-mutant and KRAS-wildtype strata, the association is less likely to be confined to one driver background. If it collapses or reverses in one stratum, the main effect would need a narrower context interpretation.\n\nThe second block refines the accepted SMARCA4-loss association with stronger SMARCA2 dependency by KRAS-mutation status. H6 and related strata are already very large and independently validated, so these KRAS-context tests ask whether the effect is robust across two major oncogenic-driver backgrounds. Plausible alternatives include context dilution, co-alteration confounding, or persistence of a broad chromatin-dependency effect.\n\nThe third block refines the accepted PTEN-loss association with stronger STAT3 dependency by KRAS-mutation status. PTEN loss has been robust in TP53-intact, TP53-loss, PIK3CA-intact, PIK3CA-mutant, and Avana-library strata. KRAS-mutant and KRAS-wildtype strata test whether another common driver background modifies the effect.\n\nThe fourth block completes the MSI-high-WRN context map in TP53-loss lines. The main MSI-high effect is huge and independently validated, and the TP53-intact stratum is accepted, but the TP53-loss cell is smaller. This is a robustness and cell-size stress test rather than a discovery of a new effect.\n\nThe fifth block adds focused mechanistic coverage for RPL11. MYC amplification can increase translational and ribosomal stress, potentially producing stronger RPL11 dependency preferentially when TP53 is intact. The full-sample MYC-RPL11 relationship is not promising enough to prioritize broadly, but the TP53-intact context is a more specific p53-dependent hypothesis.\n\nThe last three proposals test pathway-bypass and co-dependency logic around RAS and receptor tyrosine kinase dependencies. record.narrative: I selected twelve untested but previously registered comparisons that combine focused robustness checks for accepted associations with a few mechanistic follow-ups. The first six, H77-H82, test the three strongest accepted main effects across KRAS-mutant and KRAS-wildtype backgrounds: KEAP1 loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency, SMARCA4 loss versus stronger SMARCA2 dependency, and PTEN loss versus stronger STAT3 dependency. Under the registered signed convention, positive estimates support the claimed direction. These tests ask whether the large accepted associations persist across a major driver co-alteration context or collapse in one background. H83 tests MSI-high versus stronger WRN dependency among TP53-loss lines, completing the TP53-intact/TP53-loss context map for a validated effect. H15, H61, H63, and H64 add subtype and batch robustness for accepted effects: WRN in adenocarcinoma, KEAP1-NFE2L2 in batch_a and adenocarcinoma, and PTEN-STAT3 in adenocarcinoma. H84 adds a focused mechanistic test of whether MYC amplification is associated with stronger RPL11 dependency specifically in TP53-intact lines. I prioritized these over H58-H60, H35, H85-H87, and other deferred or lower-priority candidates because they target either accepted-effect context dependence or a small number of mechanistically coherent follow-ups.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All estimates were interpreted using the registered signed convention. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has more negative dependency scores and therefore stronger dependency. For direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has less negative scores and therefore weaker dependency. Positive lower bounds far from zero are taken as evidence of a scientifically meaningful association on the dependency-score scale; near-zero intervals are treated as unsupported. These remain supplied-dataset associations, not causal or clinically generalizable claims. H77 and H78 strongly support the accepted KEAP1-loss association with weaker NFE2L2 dependency in both KRAS-mutant and KRAS-wildtype contexts: signed estimates +0.805, CI [0.767,0.843], and +0.793, CI [0.769,0.817]. This makes a KRAS-background confounding explanation less plausible for the main KEAP1-NFE2L2 effect. H79 and H80 strongly support the accepted SMARCA4-loss association with stronger SMARCA2 dependency in KRAS-mutant and KRAS-wildtype strata: +0.774, CI [0.733,0.814], and +0.788, CI [0.766,0.810]. The effect is broad across both major driver contexts and remains very large relative to the SMARCA2 score distribution. H81 and H82 support the accepted PTEN-loss association with stronger STAT3 dependency in KRAS-mutant and KRAS-wildtype strata: +0.249, CI [0.139,0.358], and +0.273, CI [0.213,0.332]. The KRAS-mutant cell is smaller, but its interval is entirely positive and its lower bound still represents a substantial STAT3-dependency shift; the KRAS-wildtype stratum is precise and replicates the main effect. H83 accepts MSI-high versus stronger WRN dependency among TP53-loss lines: +0.833, CI [0.765,0.900]. The exposed cell size is only 24, but the contrast is enormous and the lower bound remains far above zero, so I accept this as stratum-specific robustness evidence rather than precise generalizable estimation. H84 does not support MYC amplification versus stronger RPL11 dependency in TP53-intact lines: signed estimate -0.009, CI [-0.034,0.015]. The point estimate is negative and the upper bound is too small to represent a clinically meaningful positive shift on the RPL11 score scale, so I reject the registered direction and close it. H15, H61, H63, and H64 complete subtype and batch robustness checks and all support accepted effects: MSI-high WRN dependency in adenocarcinoma +0.784, CI [0.748,0.820]; KEAP1 NFE2L2 in batch_a +0.812, CI [0.765,0.858]; KEAP1 NFE2L2 in adenocarcinoma +0.793, CI [0.769,0.817]; and PTEN STAT3 in adenocarcinoma +0.268, CI [0.206,0.330]. The multiplicity is substantial, but these are not borderline findings for the accepted effects: they are large, consistently signed, and lower bounds are far above trivial. The main remaining scientific weakness is that the KEAP1-NFE2L2 main claim, H13, still lacks its own independent validation despite very strong discovery and stratum robustness. I therefore request independent validation of H13.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

record.narrative: All estimates were interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. H13 now has independent validation in addition to discovery: signed estimate +0.796, 95% CI [0.776,0.816], and independent validation +0.791, independent interval [0.763,0.820]. This is a very large shift on the NFE2L2 dependency-score scale, where the full-sample mean is approximately -0.093 and SD is approximately 0.363, and it is far above any 10% practical threshold. Direction +1 means KEAP1-loss lines have less negative NFE2L2 scores, hence weaker NFE2L2 dependency. I therefore reaffirm and close H13. H7 also has validation: discovery +0.790, CI [0.760,0.819], validation +0.812, independent interval [0.765,0.858]. This is far above the WRN score SD of approximately 0.263 and supports MSI-high being associated with stronger WRN dependency in this dataset. I reaffirm and close H7. H39 failed to provide meaningful support: validation estimate was +0.00019, independent interval [-0.038,0.039], near null for RB1 loss versus POLR2A dependency. The interval is not precise enough to exclude every clinically meaningful positive effect, but there is no positive evidence that RB1 loss is associated with stronger POLR2A dependency. I leave it unresolved and closed. Overall, the strongest supported dataset associations are SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency; all now have discovery plus independent validation. Several other candidates were unsupported or failed replication, including EGFR amplification with EGFR dependency, RB1 loss with POLR2A dependency, BRAF V600E, ERBB2 amplification, and MYC-related dependency effects in several contexts. These remain associations in the supplied lung CRISPR dataset, not causal or clinically generalizable claims. Next, I propose interaction checks using Cas9 activity to ask whether the accepted effects are modified by screen-quality context, while also retaining active subtype, batch, and pathway-bypass checks for follow-up.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
All future estimates should be interpreted using the registered signed-estimate convention. For direction -1 claims, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score and therefore stronger dependency. For direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a less negative score and therefore weaker dependency. A scientifically meaningful claim should show a large effect relative to the outcome's score distribution and an interval excluding zero with a lower bound beyond a trivial shift. These remain supplied-dataset associations, not causal or clinically generalizable claims.

The new proposals shift emphasis away from the already validated accepted effects toward coherent mechanistic contexts. The first block tests the p53/proteostasis axis. RPL11 participates in p53 stabilization through MDM2, so TP53 loss may reduce dependence on RPL11; the registered direction +1 claims weaker RPL11 dependency. USP7 also interacts with p53/MDM2 regulation, and BRCA2 loss may increase dependence on USP7-mediated repair/proteostasis networks; the registered direction -1 claims stronger USP7 dependency. These are falsifiable pathway-biology hypotheses, with near-null results expected if the effect is confined to the known accepted effects.

The second block tests upstream/downstream bypass logic in RAS and receptor-tyrosine-kinase signaling. MYC amplification, PIK3CA mutation, KRAS mutation, BRAF V600E, and PTEN loss can all reduce dependence on a more upstream oncogenic node by activating parallel or downstream survival programs. Accordingly, MYC amplification is registered against weaker KRAS dependency, PIK3CA mutation against weaker ERBB2 dependency, KRAS mutation against weaker EGFR dependency, BRAF V600E against weaker RIT1 dependency, and PTEN loss against weaker BRAF dependency. Plausible alternatives include co-selection, pathway co-amplification, or no dependency change; near-zero or reversed results would be acceptable and informative.

The third block adds focused pathway coverage for less-characterized outcomes. APC alteration may alter Wnt/secretory demands, so APC mutation is registered against stronger TMED10 dependency. CDKN2A loss may increase mitotic/checkpoint stress, so it is registered against stronger KIF18A dependency. BRCA2 loss may create transcription-repair conflicts and increase dependence on POLR2A; this is registered as stronger POLR2A dependency. Each is a targeted biomarker-by-gene-dependency hypothesis rather than a broad fishing exercise.

I also made investigation-only updates for bookkeeping. H1 KRAS mutation versus KRAS dependency remains near null in discovery and is closed unresolved. Subtype interaction H35 and batch_a main-effect checks H58-H60 are deferred because accepted-effect context robustness has already been covered by validated strata and Avana-library checks; Cas9-activity interactions H88-H91 remain active because screen-quality modification is a more direct technical robustness test for accepted effects.

Iteration 6/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No new evidence is assessed in this analyze form. I selected twelve active, previously registered but untested claims to balance technical robustness for the accepted validated associations with targeted mechanistic exploration of other dependency outcomes. H88-H91 test Cas9-activity interaction for the four accepted effects: SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2, MSI-high/WRN, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2, and PTEN loss/STAT3. Under the registered direction convention, a positive interaction means the signed effect is larger in higher-Cas9 screens than in their complement; negative means it is smaller. These are direct technical-modifier tests rather than new primary discoveries, so near-zero interactions would support robustness. H92-H99 test coherent mechanistic associations: TP53 loss versus weaker RPL11 dependency, BRCA2 loss versus stronger USP7 dependency, MYC amplification versus weaker KRAS dependency, PIK3CA mutation versus weaker ERBB2 dependency, APC mutation versus stronger TMED10 dependency, CDKN2A loss versus stronger KIF18A dependency, BRAF V600E versus weaker RIT1 dependency, and KRAS mutation versus weaker EGFR dependency. H100 and H101 are not run now because they are lower-priority extensions relative to the accepted-effect Cas9 checks and the selected p53/repair/pathway-bypass tests; they can be revisited if results indicate that PTEN/BRAF or BRCA2/POLR2A axes deserve follow-up. All selected comparisons should be interpreted as dataset-specific associations, with acceptance requiring effect sizes large relative to the dependency-score scale and intervals excluding zero with nontrivial bounds.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
All newly delivered estimates were interpreted under the signed-estimate convention. For direction -1 claims, positive values mean stronger dependency or a stronger positive signed effect in the focal subgroup; for direction +1 claims, positive values mean weaker dependency or a stronger positive signed effect in the focal subgroup. For interaction claims, positive values mean the signed effect is larger in the high-Cas9 subgroup than in the complement.

The Cas9-activity interaction tests do not show a positive modification of the accepted effects. H88 SMARCA2 plus SMARCA4 loss interaction was small and positive, +0.014 [ -0.029, 0.058 ], so I leave it unresolved rather than accept it: it is not significantly positive, and the interval includes both modestly negative and modestly positive values. H89 MSI-high plus WRN interaction was negative, -0.039 [ -0.103, 0.025 ]; the upper bound is small relative to the very large accepted WRN main effect, so I reject this registered positive-interaction direction. H90 KEAP1 plus NFE2L2 interaction was tiny and positive, +0.005 [ -0.039, 0.050 ], and is unresolved. H91 PTEN plus STAT3 interaction was negative, -0.021 [ -0.132, 0.090 ]; because the upper bound could include a nontrivial positive modification, I leave it unresolved rather than reject it as precisely null. Overall, these results do not provide evidence that the accepted effects are stronger specifically in higher-Cas9 screens. They do not refute the accepted main effects because null or imprecise interaction estimates can occur when subgroup modification is small or absent; the main effects were accepted from discovery and independent validation or broad stratum replication, not from these interaction tests.

The mechanistic main-effect tests were mostly null or too small. H92 TP53 loss versus weaker RPL11 dependency gave a positive tiny estimate, +0.004 [ -0.016, 0.024 ]; I leave it unresolved because the interval is imprecise and includes possible modest effects, but the point estimate is not supportive. H93 BRCA2 loss versus stronger USP7 dependency gave +0.004 [ -0.064, 0.072 ]; this is unresolved because of imprecision, but there is no evidence supporting a meaningful positive association. H96 APC mutation versus stronger TMED10 dependency was +0.004 [ -0.020, 0.027 ], unresolved. H98 BRAF V600E versus weaker RIT1 dependency was +0.004 [ -0.025, 0.033 ], unresolved. These leave the biological interpretation uncertain but do not establish new associations.

Several tests point opposite to the registered direction and have intervals that do not leave room for a scientifically meaningful positive effect. H94 MYC amplification versus weaker KRAS dependency gave -0.010 [ -0.032, 0.012 ]; the upper bound is small relative to the KRAS score SD, so I reject the positive direction. H95 PIK3CA mutation versus weaker ERBB2 dependency gave -0.004 [ -0.024, 0.017 ]; this is too small to support the claimed weaker ERBB2 dependency. H97 CDKN2A loss versus stronger KIF18A dependency gave -0.013 [ -0.033, 0.006 ], a small negative estimate; reject. H99 KRAS mutation versus weaker EGFR dependency gave -0.010 [ -0.027, 0.008 ]; reject. These null or opposite results argue against the proposed upstream/downstream bypass or mitotic-stress associations in this dataset, though they do not imply those biology is impossible generally.

Because no newly tested claim is strong enough to accept, I request independent validation only for H83. H83 is an accepted but small-cell stratum-specific robustness result: MSI-high versus stronger WRN dependency among TP53-loss lines, +0.833 [0.765,0.900] with only 24 exposed lines. Validating H83 is useful because it could confirm a large stratum effect or reveal that the accepted WRN association is unstable in that small TP53-loss subset. This does not affect the main validated MSI-high WRN effect, H7, but it would clarify whether the stratum-specific acceptance was driven by imprecise small-sample estimation.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.
